Section 20 of 16 USC provides a further statement of the basic purpose of the national parks:
... these areas [the national park system] are united through their interrelated purposes and resources into one national park system ... preserved and managed for the benefit and inspiration of all the people of the United States.
These statutes make improper any use of the parks that impairs their basic natural resources. Although the draft statement leaves no doubt that ORV use does substantially impair resources wherever it is allowed,* the Secretary's memo states that ORV areas will be allowed in the Park System if the bureau head determines that "off-road vehicle use ... will not adversely affect ... natural, aesthetic, or scenic values." This is plainly inconsistent with the Draft Statement's declaration that ORV use always adversely affects natural values. Consequently, the Secretary should change his memo to require that ORVs be banned from national park lands.
Recreational use within the National Wildlife Refuge System is controlled by 16 USC 460k. That section provides that recreational use within the refuge system or in other conservation areas administered by the Secretary of the Interior for fish and wildlife purposes, will be allowed if such use can be made compatible with the primary purpose of the conservation areas, and can be an appropriate secondary or incidental use.
